narrative.overview:
The Antseed system makes a narrowing process visible. Connected bands show how one company becomes a ranked, reachable lead set.

The visual language is calm, exact, and operational. Pixel headings add Antseed character. Flat rails, dotted edges, and direct copy keep the work traceable.

This surface extends the existing Antseed identity. It preserves the lockup, Geist families, green controls, dotted rails, and day and night themes.
keyCharacteristics: A centered rail contains the complete workspace.
Eight-pixel dot grids define page and section edges.
Pixel type marks headings and key figures.
Green marks action, readiness, progress, and focus.
Connected stage widths show pipeline narrowing.
Day and night themes keep the same hierarchy.

rules.name: The Green Means Progress Rule
rules.body: Use green for action, focus, readiness, success, and measured progress.

rules.name: The Theme Role Rule
rules.body: Change token values between themes. Do not change component hierarchy or meaning.

rules.name: The Acid Rarity Rule
rules.body: Keep acid green out of normal controls. Reserve it for text selection.

rules.name: The Pixel Anchor Rule
rules.body: Use Geist Pixel for headings and important figures. Do not use it for dense body text.

rules.name: The Data Voice Rule
rules.body: Use mono type only when the content behaves like data, code, or system output.

rules.name: The One Rail Rule
rules.body: Keep the complete task inside one continuous rail. Do not split it into dashboard islands.

rules.name: The Narrowing Rule
rules.body: Keep all five stages connected, ordered, and visibly narrower when counts fall.

rules.name: The Flat First Rule
rules.body: Use tone and hairlines before shadow. Add lift only for action or hover feedback.

rules.name: The Soft Precision Rule
rules.body: Use moderate curves for controls and surfaces. Do not use oversized rounded containers.

dos: Do preserve the Antseed lockup, pixel headings, dotted rails, and both themes.
Do show every stage, gate, count, failure, and output in sequence.
Do use green consistently for action, focus, readiness, and success.
Do keep paid enrichment behind a clear confirmation step.
Do respect reduced-motion settings and visible keyboard focus.
Do keep direct product language and real data labels.
donts: Don't turn the workspace into unrelated dashboard cards.
Don't hide a failed gate or let later stages appear complete after failure.
Don't use the pixel font for paragraphs, form values, or dense tables.
Don't use acid green as a normal button or surface color.
Don't replace dotted structure with heavy borders or large shadows.
Don't change the hierarchy between day and night themes.
